doctrine: Recipes and typed artifact facts are sole policy and topology authorities. Compiled ordered bindings own repeated execution. Each wave migrates every caller and deletes displaced selectors, synthetic identities, copied policy, wrappers, and test-only production runtime code. No compatibility path or parallel API remains. Preserve numerical behavior and hard-fail on absent authority. Production code must be net-negative unless an unavoidable schema migration provides greater immediate deletion.

items.title: Make typed artifact profiles select generation recipes

steps.title: Replace image family probe chains and platform duplicates with one profile-driven capability compiler
steps.rationale: Runtime recipes cannot be authoritative while command discovery still selects them through family-specific Recognize and IsPipeline branches. Compile inventory once, resolve typed declarations, migrate all callers, and delete the branch chains.

steps.title: Replace model-only inventory ownership and queries with a tensor-bearing artifact contract
steps.rationale: Tensor inventory validation accepts projectors while the schema and lookup API still claim model-only ownership. Publish one owner contract and delete kind-specific handling.

items.title: Retain compiled graph and indexed input ownership

steps.title: Migrate repeated CUDA graph execution from pointer maps and per-call compilation to indexed programs
steps.rationale: Ordered diffusion bindings are converted back to maps and Feeds.Execute recompiles output graphs. Retain compiled slots for repeated execution; keep maps only at the reference-executor boundary.

items.title: Delete displaced runtime and wrapper surface

steps.title: Delete test-only diffusion programs, redundant recipe wrappers, and duplicate profile bootstrap plumbing
steps.rationale: Production files still contain test-only graph executors, one-line capability wrappers, and command-local profile publication. Migrate consumers to the authorities established by prior waves and delete the old objects.
